precepts.text: And thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children. Teach them what? The laws of God. And shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thine house, and when thou walkest by the way, and when thou liest down. It is a routine of the word. It's repetition.
precepts.point: If we want to strengthen our families: one, husbands be in order, wife be in order, children, they will learn how to obey the Lord by your behavior, and in turn they're putting on the whole armor of God.

note.label: Making the Great Red Dragon's 8th Head 'great Again'

precepts.why:
“And thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children”. Teach them what? The laws of God. “and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thine house, and when thou walkest by the way, and when thou liest down, and when thou risest up.”

It is a routine of the word. It's repetition: sitting in the house, walking by the way, lying down, rising up. Children are not mature enough to make that cognitive decision on their own; the parent has to put the law in them diligently, over and over.

That is how the children put on the whole armour of God. The husband in order, the wife in order, the time redeemed, and the laws taught diligently at every part of the day, so the house can “stand against the wiles of the devil.”

precepts.text: Beware lest thou forget the Lord, which brought thee forth out of the land of Egypt. That's why you do it. Now if you forget the Lord, guess what? You're going to be tempted.
precepts.point: If we want to strengthen our families: one, husbands be in order, wife be in order, children, they will learn how to obey the Lord by your behavior, and in turn they're putting on the whole armor of God.

note.label: Making the Great Red Dragon's 8th Head 'great Again'

precepts.why:
“Then beware lest thou forget the Lord, which brought thee forth out of the land of Egypt, from the house of bondage.”

That's why you do it: why you teach the laws diligently to the children, talk of them in the house and by the way, and sing the psalms and spiritual songs over and over. The repetition keeps the house from forgetting the Lord who brought us out of the house of bondage.

Now if you forget the Lord, guess what? You're going to be tempted. Forgetting the Lord leaves the armour off, and the wiles of the devil find a way in. Remembering him is how the family puts on the whole armour of God and stands.

precepts.text: Ye shall not tempt the Lord your God. Well, how don't you tempt him? Teach them diligently. Husband in order, wife in order, redeeming the time. Ye shall diligently keep the commandments of the Lord your God: that's how you do it, is instructing them.
precepts.point: If we want to strengthen our families: one, husbands be in order, wife be in order, children, they will learn how to obey the Lord by your behavior, and in turn they're putting on the whole armor of God.

note.label: Making the Great Red Dragon's 8th Head 'great Again'

precepts.why:
“Ye shall not tempt the Lord your God, as ye tempted him in Massah. Ye shall diligently keep the commandments of the Lord your God, and his testimonies, and his statutes, which he hath commanded thee.”

Well, how don't you tempt him? Teach them diligently. Husband in order, wife in order, redeeming the time. Diligently keeping the commandments, testimonies and statutes: that's how you do it, by instructing them.

So all these scriptures go together. Do half of them and you have only pieces of the armour. Do them all, in the house, with the children, and the family has put on the whole armour of God, “that ye may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil.”

precepts.text: And it shall be our righteousness, if we observe to do all these commandments before the Lord our God, as he hath commanded us. That is what righteousness is.
precepts.point: And such were some of you: everybody in here can identify with something on that list and say, I used to do that. But ye are washed, but ye are sanctified, but ye are justified in the name of the Lord Jesus, and by the Spirit of our God. We are washed with the word of God.

note.label: The Negro Community: A Wasteland of Tears

precepts.why:
“Know ye not that the unrighteous shall not inherit the kingdom of God?” To know who the unrighteous are, you have to know what righteousness is, and the law defines it: “And it shall be our righteousness, if we observe to do all these commandments before the Lord our God, as he hath commanded us.”

That is what righteousness is: observing to do all the commandments before the Lord, as he commanded. So the unrighteous who will not inherit the kingdom are those who will not do the commandments.

That is the problem with Christianity. It is not that the Lord's arm is too short or his ear too heavy; it is that your sins have separated between you and your God. They are not trying to transform their lives to that of the nation of Israel according to the holy scriptures. And that is why Paul lists fornicators, idolaters, adulterers and the rest: every one of them breaks the commandments that are our righteousness.

precepts.text: Christ said, I and my Father are one. Is there a division between Christ and his Father? No, they are on one accord.
precepts.point: Hear, O Israel: the Lord our God is one Lord. We start with the order first. We as a body have to be one, in unison, in sync. This is why we have been able to accomplish the amazing things we have in this congregation: because we are one.

note.label: Member's In The Body

precepts.why:
“Hear, O Israel: The Lord our God is one Lord.” One mind, one body: we start with the order first. The Lord our God is one Lord, and Christ shows what that oneness looks like: “I and my Father are one.”

Is there a division between Christ and his Father? No. They are on one accord. Two persons, the Father and the Son, and yet one, because the Son is in full agreement with the Father.

That is what we as a body have to be: one, in unison, in sync. This is why we have been able to accomplish the amazing things we have in this body, in this congregation: because we are one. Many of our people today have a social religion, more like a superstition, believing what society told them to do. We rely on the scriptures and believe on the Lord as it is written, and the scripture says the Lord is one and Christ is one with him.

precepts.text: I can of mine own self do nothing: as I hear, I judge: and my judgment is just; because I seek not mine own will, but the will of the Father which hath sent me. Christ does not do what he wants to; he does what the Father tells him to. Yet the scripture says he and his Father are one.
precepts.point: Hear, O Israel: the Lord our God is one Lord. We start with the order first. We as a body have to be one, in unison, in sync. This is why we have been able to accomplish the amazing things we have in this congregation: because we are one.

note.label: Member's In The Body

precepts.why:
How are Christ and the Father one? Christ does what his Father tells him to do. “I can of mine own self do nothing”: Christ said it himself. “as I hear, I judge”: as I'm told, that's what I do. “and my judgment is just”: the things he does are justified, “because I seek not mine own will, but the will of the Father which hath sent me.”

He didn't do what he wanted to do; he did what the Father told him to do. You see how that works? He says, I don't do what I want to, I do what the Father tells me to, and yet the scripture says he and his Father are one.

That is the oneness of Deuteronomy 6:4. Being one is not everybody doing their own will; it is every member doing the will of the one who is over him. That is how Christ is one with the Father, and how the body is one with Christ.

precepts.text: At that day ye shall know that I am in my Father, and ye in me, and I in you. Christ does what his Father tells him to do, and Christ tells us what to do, and we keep those commandments; all of them, not picking and choosing and cherry picking like Christians. He that hath my commandments, and keepeth them, he it is that loveth me; and I will love him, and will manifest myself to him. He is explaining how you receive the Holy Spirit: in order to have the Holy Spirit, you must be one with the Most High and his son.
precepts.point: Hear, O Israel: the Lord our God is one Lord. We start with the order first. We as a body have to be one, in unison, in sync. This is why we have been able to accomplish the amazing things we have in this congregation: because we are one.

note.label: Member's In The Body

precepts.why:
Christ warned of his departure, when he would no longer be with them in the body: “At that day ye shall know that I am in my Father, and ye in me, and I in you.” What does it mean? Christ does what his Father tells him to do, Christ comes and tells us what to do, and we keep those commandments.

“He that hath my commandments, and keepeth them, he it is that loveth me.” What commandments? The Father's commandments, all of them. We ain't Christians up in here picking and choosing and cherry picking, hopping and skipping around. Everything the Father told us to do: those are the commandments. The one who has them and keeps them is the man or woman that loves Christ, that loves the Lord.

“and he that loveth me shall be loved of my Father, and I will love him, and will manifest myself to him.” He is explaining the manifestation, how you receive the Holy Spirit. In order to have the Holy Spirit, you must be one with the Most High God and his Son.

That is how we keep the first commandment, to “love the Lord thy God with all thine heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy might”: by keeping his commandments, and being one with the Father and the Son as they are one.

precepts.text: It shall be our righteousness if we observe to do all these commandments; righteousness goes into keeping the laws.
precepts.point: Righteousness is immortal, and righteousness is defined by the law: it shall be our righteousness if we observe to do all these commandments. Abram's faith showed itself in his works.

note.label: Genesis 15: The Covenant and the Four Hundred Years

precepts.why:
What is righteousness? The scriptures define it, and it is defined by the law: “it shall be our righteousness, if we observe to do all these commandments before the Lord our God, as he hath commanded us.”

So when Abram believed and “he counted it to him for righteousness”, that righteousness goes into keeping the laws. Abram’s faith was not a feeling; it showed itself in his works, in observing to do what the Lord commanded him.

precepts.text: To the law and to the testimony: if they speak not according to this word, it is because there is no light in them.
precepts.point: Thou shalt do that which is right and good in the sight of the Lord: not by personal standards of what feels good in the heart, but by the standard set before us, for the scripture says plainly that the law is good. The reward is to go in and possess the good land, the real wealth, not the bags and rings and sneakers, which are vanity.

note.label: Deuteronomy 6: Teach Them Diligently unto Thy Children

precepts.why:
“To the law and to the testimony: if they speak not according to this word, it is because there is no light in them.”

Testimony is one of the trigger words that confuses our people. The laws are what Moses gave, and the testimonies are the history of the forefathers and foremothers, what they went through and how it was handled according to the laws. Everything correlates: when king David had Uriah killed, that goes back to thou shalt not kill, thou shalt not covet, and bearing false witness; he was dealing with much sin in that one matter. That is how you go precept upon precept, line upon line, to the law and to the testimony.

So a personal testimony that cannot come back to the Bible is not biblical. If they speak not according to this word, it is because there is no light, no truth, in them. That is why Israel is to “diligently keep the commandments of the Lord your God, and his testimonies, and his statutes”.

precepts.text: The commandment is a lamp, and the law is light; that is the light that is missing in them that speak not according to the word.
precepts.point: Thou shalt do that which is right and good in the sight of the Lord: not by personal standards of what feels good in the heart, but by the standard set before us, for the scripture says plainly that the law is good. The reward is to go in and possess the good land, the real wealth, not the bags and rings and sneakers, which are vanity.

note.label: Deuteronomy 6: Teach Them Diligently unto Thy Children

precepts.why:
“For the commandment is a lamp; and the law is light; and reproofs of instruction are the way of life”. That is the light that is missing in them that speak not according to the word.

Isaiah says if they speak not according to the law and the testimony there is no light in them; Solomon shows what that light is, the commandment and the law. A testimony that cannot come back to the commandments has no lamp. Diligently keep the commandments, the testimonies and the statutes, and you walk in the light.

precepts.text: Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path.
precepts.point: Thou shalt do that which is right and good in the sight of the Lord: not by personal standards of what feels good in the heart, but by the standard set before us, for the scripture says plainly that the law is good. The reward is to go in and possess the good land, the real wealth, not the bags and rings and sneakers, which are vanity.

note.label: Deuteronomy 6: Teach Them Diligently unto Thy Children

precepts.why:
“Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path.” The word is the light: the commandment is a lamp and the law is light, and when they speak not according to this word it is because there is no light in them.

So the standard for “that which is right and good in the sight of the Lord” is the word set before us, not personal standards of what feels good in the heart. The word lights the path, and at the end of it is the reward, to go in and possess the good land.

precepts.text: He that saith, I know him, and keepeth not his commandments, is a liar, and the truth is not in him; the same measure as no light in them.
precepts.point: Thou shalt do that which is right and good in the sight of the Lord: not by personal standards of what feels good in the heart, but by the standard set before us, for the scripture says plainly that the law is good. The reward is to go in and possess the good land, the real wealth, not the bags and rings and sneakers, which are vanity.

note.label: Deuteronomy 6: Teach Them Diligently unto Thy Children

precepts.why:
“He that saith, I know him, and keepeth not his commandments, is a liar, and the truth is not in him.” The same measure as no light in them.

Isaiah says if they speak not according to the law and the testimony there is no light in them; John says if a man keeps not his commandments the truth is not in him. No light, no truth. A personal testimony that cannot come back to the Bible is not biblical, and a man who says he knows him but does not keep the commandments is a liar. Diligently keeping the commandments, testimonies and statutes is how the truth is in you.

precepts.text: The law is holy, and the commandment holy, and just, and good.
precepts.point: Thou shalt do that which is right and good in the sight of the Lord: not by personal standards of what feels good in the heart, but by the standard set before us, for the scripture says plainly that the law is good. The reward is to go in and possess the good land, the real wealth, not the bags and rings and sneakers, which are vanity.

note.label: Deuteronomy 6: Teach Them Diligently unto Thy Children

precepts.why:
“Wherefore the law is holy, and the commandment holy, and just, and good.” The scripture says plainly that the law is good.

So doing “that which is right and good in the sight of the Lord” is doing the law, not what feels good in the heart. Paul and Moses agree: the commandment is holy, just and good, and diligently keeping it is what it means to do right and good, with the good land as the reward.

precepts.text: Blessed are they that keep judgment, and he that doeth righteousness at all times; at all times, not one day a week.
precepts.point: Words like testimony, righteousness, grace, and faith must be defined out of the scripture itself: the Bible is a dictionary within itself. Egypt means slavery, righteousness means keeping the laws, and going by the Bible's own definitions destroys the private interpretations of the religions.

note.label: Deuteronomy 6: Teach Them Diligently unto Thy Children

precepts.why:
“Blessed are they that keep judgment, and he that doeth righteousness at all times.” At all times, not one day a week.

“And it shall be our righteousness, if we observe to do all these commandments before the Lord our God”. Keeping the commandments is what makes you righteous, and righteousness is kept at all times, the fringes worn seven days a week and not on the sabbath only.

Righteousness is defined out of the scripture itself, for the Bible is a dictionary within itself. Righteousness means keeping the laws, and going by the Bible's own definitions destroys the private interpretations of the religions.

precepts.text: My tongue shall speak of thy word: for all thy commandments are righteousness.
precepts.point: Words like testimony, righteousness, grace, and faith must be defined out of the scripture itself: the Bible is a dictionary within itself. Egypt means slavery, righteousness means keeping the laws, and going by the Bible's own definitions destroys the private interpretations of the religions.

note.label: Deuteronomy 6: Teach Them Diligently unto Thy Children

precepts.why:
“My tongue shall speak of thy word: for all thy commandments are righteousness.” That is the Bible defining its own word: righteousness is the commandments.

Moses says the same: “it shall be our righteousness, if we observe to do all these commandments before the Lord our God, as he hath commanded us.” Words like testimony, righteousness, grace and faith must be defined out of the scripture itself, for the Bible is a dictionary within itself. Egypt means slavery, righteousness means keeping the laws, and going by the Bible's own definitions destroys the private interpretations of the religions.

So when the son asks what the testimonies, statutes and judgments mean, the answer starts with the history, “We were Pharaoh’s bondmen in Egypt”, and ends here: all his commandments are righteousness, kept at all times, for our good always.

precepts.text: It shall be our righteousness if we observe to do all these commandments before the Lord.
precepts.point: To be righteous is to observe to do all the commandments of the Lord; all unrighteousness is sin, and sin is the transgression of the law. David was righteous and did not want to war against his own son, yet good was repaid to him, while the sinner was pursued by his own evil.

note.label: 2 Samuel 17: The Counsel of the Lord Shall Stand

precepts.why:
“And it shall be our righteousness, if we observe to do all these commandments before the Lord our God, as he hath commanded us.”

That is what it means to be righteous: to observe to do all the commandments of the Lord. So when the scripture says good shall be repaid to the righteous, this is who it means. David was righteous and good was repaid to him, while Ahithophel the sinner was pursued by his own evil until he hanged himself.

precepts.text: Righteousness is when we observe to do all these commandments.
precepts.point: Righteousness is defined by keeping the commandments.

note.label: Psalm 15: Who Shall Abide in the Tabernacle

precepts.why: “Lord, who shall abide in thy tabernacle? who shall dwell in thy holy hill?” The answer is the man that walketh uprightly and worketh righteousness and speaketh the truth in his heart. Righteousness is defined by keeping the commandments: “And it shall be our righteousness, if we observe to do all these commandments before the Lord our God, as he hath commanded us.” To work righteousness is to observe to do all these commandments.

precepts.text: Righteousness is observing to do all these commandments before the Most High as He commanded us.
precepts.point: If we are doing the righteousness of the Most High, which is keeping His commandments, we will not be put to shame, and that is why David prays this thing.

note.label: Psalm 31: In Thee O Lord Do I Put My Trust

precepts.why:
David prays “deliver me in thy righteousness”, and asks “let me never be ashamed”. Moses shows what the righteousness of the Most High is: “it shall be our righteousness, if we observe to do all these commandments before the Lord our God, as he hath commanded us.” Righteousness is keeping his commandments.

This is a psalm of David dealing with his commitment to the Most High. If we are doing the righteousness of the Most High, which is keeping his commandments, we will not be put to shame, and that is why David prays this thing.

precepts.text: It shall be our righteousness if we observe to do all these commandments as He commanded.
precepts.point: The way to get the Most High to hear our prayers is righteousness. His eyes are over the righteous and His ears are open to their prayers, but His face is against them that do evil.

note.label: Psalm 55: Cast Thy Burden Upon the Lord

precepts.why: What is righteousness? “And it shall be our righteousness, if we observe to do all these commandments before the Lord our God, as he hath commanded us.” It shall be our righteousness if we observe to do all these commandments as he commanded. The eyes of the Lord are over the righteous and his ears open to their prayers, so keeping the commandments is how our prayer gets his ear. That is how David could ask the Most High to attend unto him and hear him.

precepts.text: It shall be our righteousness if we observe to do all these commandments; righteousness is keeping God's commandments.
precepts.point: He cometh to judge the earth: with righteousness shall He judge the world and the people with equity. Righteousness means us keeping God's commandments, observing and doing them, and equity means justice, the practice of giving what is due. By His righteousness He is going to give the people the justice due to them.

note.label: Psalm 98: Sing Unto the Lord a New Song

precepts.why:
With righteousness shall he judge the world. What is righteousness? “And it shall be our righteousness, if we observe to do all these commandments before the Lord our God, as he hath commanded us.” Righteousness is us keeping God's commandments, observing and doing them.

So when he comes to judge the earth, the standard he judges by is the commandments.

precepts.text: We are commanded to teach our children the words of the Most High diligently.
precepts.point: The covenant is to such as keep His commandments and remember them to do them. To do them is an action word.

note.label: Psalm 103: Bless the Lord for His Benefits to Israel

precepts.why:
“But the mercy of the Lord is from everlasting to everlasting upon them that fear him, and his righteousness unto children’s children”. His righteousness reaches children's children, and this is why we must teach our children in every generation, so they receive that same mercy.

The law commands it: “And these words, which I command thee this day, shall be in thine heart: And thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children, and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thine house, and when thou walkest by the way, and when thou liest down, and when thou risest up.” We are commanded to teach our children the words of the Most High diligently, in the house, by the way, lying down and rising up.

Man's days are as grass, but the mercy is from everlasting to everlasting on such as keep his covenant. The children must be taught the commandments so that they keep them and the mercy carries on to them.

precepts.text: To be converted you must be keeping God's righteousness, His commandments.
precepts.point: Zion shall be redeemed with judgment, and to be converted you have to be keeping God's laws, His righteousness. When you forsake the Lord's laws you are consumed together with the sinners.

note.label: Psalm 107: O Give Thanks unto the Lord

precepts.why:
Isaiah says Zion's converts are redeemed “with righteousness”, and Deuteronomy defines the righteousness: “it shall be our righteousness, if we observe to do all these commandments before the Lord our God, as he hath commanded us.”

So to be converted you have to be keeping God's laws, his righteousness. That is what makes a man one of the redeemed of the Lord who can say so.

precepts.text: It shall be our righteousness if we observe to do all these commandments.
precepts.point: Righteousness goes into the commandments. That is how we get salvation, the kingdom of heaven, eternal life.

note.label: Psalm 132: The Oath to David and the Throne Forever

precepts.why: “And it shall be our righteousness, if we observe to do all these commandments before the Lord our God, as he hath commanded us.” Righteousness goes into the commandments. The priests clothed with salvation teach our lost people that salvation comes by doing the righteousness of this book, and this is what that righteousness is: observing to do all these commandments.

precepts.text: It shall be our righteousness if we observe to do all these commandments before the Most High; He judges the earth in righteousness according to the law.
precepts.point: With righteousness He judges the poor and reproves with equity for the meek of the earth, smiting the earth with the rod of His mouth and slaying the wicked with the breath of His lips. Righteousness and faithfulness are the girdle of His loins.

note.label: Isaiah 11: The Rod of Jesse and the Second Gathering

precepts.why:
The rod out of the stem of Jesse is Christ, and “with righteousness shall he judge the poor, and reprove with equity for the meek of the earth”. What is righteousness? “And it shall be our righteousness, if we observe to do all these commandments before the Lord our God, as he hath commanded us.”

He judges the earth in righteousness according to the law. That is why “he shall not judge after the sight of his eyes, neither reprove after the hearing of his ears”: the Most High does not look at the stature; He judges us according to the law. Righteousness, the keeping of the commandments, is the girdle of His loins.

precepts.text: It shall be our righteousness to keep the commandments; that straight gate is the law, turning neither to the left nor the right.
precepts.point: The gates are opened that the righteous nation which keepeth the truth may enter in, and that nation is the remnant that keeps the commandments. Whose mind is stayed on the Most High is kept in perfect peace because he trusteth in Him.

note.label: Isaiah 26: A Song of Salvation and the Straight Gate

precepts.why:
“And it shall be our righteousness, if we observe to do all these commandments before the Lord our God, as he hath commanded us.” It is our righteousness to keep the commandments, and that is what makes “the righteous nation which keepeth the truth” righteous.

That straight gate the righteous enter is the law, turning neither to the left nor the right. The nation that keeps it enters the strong city, and whose mind is stayed on the Most High is kept in perfect peace, because he trusteth in Him.

precepts.text: The commandment Christ was quoting, word for word out of the law.
precepts.point: The scribe answered discreetly, and was told, Thou art not far from the kingdom of God, and no man after that durst ask him any question.

note.label: Mark 12: The Husbandmen, the Tribute, and the First Commandment

precepts.why:
Asked which is the first commandment of all, Christ answered word for word out of the law: “Hear, O Israel: The Lord our God is one Lord: And thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thine heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy might.” The first of all the commandments is that the Lord our God is one Lord, and to love him with all thy heart, soul and strength.

Loving him is keeping his commandments. And the second is like it, “Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.” Loving your neighbour as yourself means holding him to those commandments as you hold yourself, because the wages of sin is death and you do not want to see your brother die. “There is none other commandment greater than these.”

The scribe answered discreetly, that to love him and his neighbour “is more than all whole burnt offerings and sacrifices”, and was told, “Thou art not far from the kingdom of God.” After that no man durst ask him any question.

precepts.text: Thou shalt fear the Lord thy God, and serve him, and shalt swear by his name.
precepts.point: Get thee behind me, Satan: for it is written, Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and him only shalt thou serve. Again the answer is a commandment.

note.label: Luke 4: The Temptation and the Reading at Nazareth

precepts.why:
The devil showed him “all the kingdoms of the world in a moment of time.” No man can do that, which settles who was standing there. Then the offer: “All this power will I give thee, and the glory of them: for that is delivered unto me; and to whomsoever I will I give it. If thou therefore wilt worship me, all shall be thine.” The offer is real, and the price is worship.

“Get thee behind me, Satan: for it is written, Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and him only shalt thou serve.” Again the answer is a commandment, and this is the one: “Thou shalt fear the Lord thy God, and serve him, and shalt swear by his name.” The Lord thy God is the one to fear and serve, him only. Christ would not take the kingdoms of the world at the price of breaking that commandment, and he put the devil behind him with it.

precepts.text: It shall be our righteousness if we observe to do all these commandments before the Most High.
precepts.point: Grace covers the thorn you sincerely fight, not the sin you commit wilfully; there is a level of perfection the Most High looks for by generation, and not every man is given the same measure.

note.label: Acts 5: All Things Common, and We Ought to Obey God Rather Than Men

precepts.why:
What is the righteousness grace reigns through? “And it shall be our righteousness, if we observe to do all these commandments before the Lord our God, as he hath commanded us.”

Righteousness is observing to do the commandments. So grace through righteousness is grace through keeping the law, the opposite of the licence to sin the church hands out.
